title: QServe: W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
problem: INT4 weight quantization methods targeting edge/single-batch inference do not translate to throughput gains in cloud LLM serving because dequantizing INT4 weights or partial sums on CUDA cores introduces 20-90% runtime overhead that erases memory bandwidth savings at large batch sizes.
motivation: Cloud LLM serving is bottlenecked by low-throughput CUDA core operations during dequantization, not solely by memory bandwidth. W8A8 kernels using Tensor Cores are efficient at large batch, but 8-bit KV cache is still memory-heavy. W4A8KV4 could combine the best of both, but requires careful algorithm and system co-design to avoid dequantization overhead on CUDA cores.
method: QServe makes INT4-quantized weights efficient by keeping dequantization on Tensor Cores (specialized multipliers) rather than general-purpose CUDA cores. Progressive group quantization uses a protective range of [-119, 119] to ensure INT4 values remain safe when scaled back to INT8 for Tensor Core multiply-accumulate without overflow; SmoothAttention suppresses outliers in Key tensors by applying per-channel scales that absorb into preceding layer weights (exploiting RoPE's mathematical commutativity), enabling 4-bit Key/Value quantization without accuracy loss. Compute-aware weight reordering stores weights in their actual GEMM access order for efficient 128-bit/thread memory fetches, while fast dequantization via vadd4 instructions (processing 4 weights per instruction) reduces per-element operations from 5 to 2 in attention decoding.
key_novelty: Three techniques—protective-range quantization for Tensor Core safety, RoPE-based Key scale pre-absorption for quantization without loss, and compute-aware weight reordering for bulk memory access—enable INT4 serving without CUDA core dequantization overhead.
contributions: QoQ W4A8KV4 quantization algorithm with protective range [-119,119] for safe INT8 Tensor Core use
Progressive group quantization: INT8 per-channel then INT4 per-group in two stages
SmoothAttention: per-channel Key scaling absorbed into preceding linear weight with RoPE commutativity
Compute-aware weight reordering for 128-bit/thread memory transactions in W4A8 GEMM
Fast dequantization via subtraction-after-multiplication order and vadd4 register-level parallelism
KV4 attention with bit-trick dequantization reducing ops from 5 to 2 per element

metrics.llama3_8b_throughput_a100: 1.2x Llama-3-8B max serving throughput on A100 vs TensorRT-LLM
metrics.llama3_8b_throughput_l40s: 1.4x Llama-3-8B max serving throughput on L40S vs TensorRT-LLM
metrics.qwen15_72b_throughput_a100: 2.4x Qwen1.5-72B throughput on A100 vs TensorRT-LLM
metrics.qwen15_72b_throughput_l40s: 3.5x Qwen1.5-72B throughput on L40S vs TensorRT-LLM
metrics.l40s_vs_a100: QServe on L40S achieves higher throughput than TensorRT-LLM FP16 on A100

limitations: Protective range [-119,119] for INT8 reduces effective quantization range slightly vs naive INT8
SmoothAttention requires per-layer calibration to determine per-channel Key scales
Compute-aware weight reordering is non-trivial to implement and hardware-specific
KV4 accuracy on tasks with high attention score variance not fully characterized
Only demonstrated on dense transformer models; MoE and hybrid models not evaluated
